title: Week in Orbit
summary: This week, the space industry is buzzing with fresh funding rounds and new partnerships, while the Space Force continues to invest in navigation and resilience. Meanwhile, the hypersonic program remains in a holding pattern, much like a plane circling the airport.

themes.title: Funding Flurry in Space
themes.body: Star Catcher and True Anomaly have both secured significant investments, signaling a growing interest in in-orbit infrastructure and data services. This influx of capital suggests investors are keen to capitalize on the burgeoning market for space resources.

themes.title: Space Force's Strategic Moves
themes.body: With a $4 million award to TrustPoint for LEO navigation and an additional $1.4 billion earmarked for space resilience in the FY27 budget, the Space Force is clearly doubling down on its operational capabilities. These investments reflect a strategic pivot towards enhancing situational awareness and navigation in increasingly crowded orbits.

themes.title: Testing Times for Hypersonics
themes.body: The hypersonic glide-vehicle program has once again slipped its testing schedule, marking the third consecutive quarter of delays. This raises questions about the program's viability and the broader implications for U.S. defense capabilities in a rapidly evolving threat landscape.

themes.title: New Players in the Game
themes.body: As Anduril and L3Harris team up for a tactical SDA constellation bid, the competitive landscape is shifting with new entrants looking to disrupt traditional aerospace dynamics. This collaboration hints at a trend where established defense contractors are increasingly partnering with tech innovators to stay relevant.
